restoration_note: Catechetical foundation-laying for the Mind of Light through five confessional sayings: unnameable Father, Third Ambassador / Father of Life, living law of sweetness and bitterness, Mother's redemptive gift of the king of light into Enmity, and the Grand-Man unity of all in one living body. Gaps tied to fixed lexicon titles (Third Ambassador, Father of Life, members) and editor-confirmed traces (their substance) restored with high confidence; surviving plural ending -ⲏⲩⲉ in §649 yields ⲙⲉⲗⲏⲩⲉ exactly. Heavily damaged middle passages (§§634, 642–647) where verbs of the Mother's action and connective phrasing cannot be reconstructed without invention have been left unrestored.

restorations.basis: Lexicon-fixed: 'Mind of Light' = ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ. The English of the line confirms the term; the spiritual arc is explicit ('foundation for the Mind of Light').

Surviving ⲡⲛⲟ- and the teaching's own structure: third of the five sayings is named ⲡⲛⲟⲙⲟⲥ (§641). Pairing 'Mind of Light and the Law' fits the catechesis (the receptive mind plus its discriminating principle), but parallel pairing is not certain.
Only a stray ⲕ survives; no apparatus, no traces, no syntactic anchor. Honest non-restoration is required.

ⲡⲧⲱ- could begin several distinct words (ⲡⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ 'Call', ⲡⲧⲱⲣ 'seal', ⲡⲧⲱϣ 'boundary'). The next sentence already supplies the Father's epithet 'unnameable', so {3} is a separate descriptor that the surrounding text does not constrain.

restorations.proposed_english: one able to give him a name
restorations.basis: Local context 'ⲡⲉⲧⲉ ⲙⲧⲉ ⲗⲁⲩⲉ {4}' = 'who has no one [to] {4}' followed by 'ⲧⲛⲉⲥ ⲙ̄ⲡⲉϩⲣⲉⲛ' ('… give him his name') reconstructs as a 'no one is able to give him a name' clause — confessing the Father precisely under the saying that he cannot be named (Father of Greatness as inmost Divine Esse).
ⲡⲙⲁⲥⲥⲛⲉⲩ ('the second') needs a head noun. §632 supplies the controlled vocabulary: ⲛ̄ⲥⲉⲭⲉ ('sayings'). 'The second saying' is exactly the structural marker the catechesis requires here.
Lexicon-fixed Manichaean title ⲡⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲙ̄ⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ = 'the Third Ambassador'. The editor's bare ϣⲁⲙⲧ is corrected to the full ordinal form ⲡⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ standard in the corpus.

restorations.proposed_english: and the Living Spirit, the Father
restorations.basis: The reading explicitly equates the second saying with the Ambassador read together with the Living Spirit / Father of Life (the next phrase being 'of Life — whom they call "the Father of Life"'). ~22 chars matches ⲙⲛ̄ ⲡⲡⲛⲁ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ ⲡⲓⲱⲧ. Plausible but other phrasings of the same idea fit equally.
Lexicon-fixed title ⲡⲓⲱⲧ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄ = 'Father of Life'. ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄ is exactly 4 chars matching est_chars=4. The reading names this title verbatim.
Only 'slight traces' reported and 6 chars; the third saying could be qualified in several ways (ⲙⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄, ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ̄, ϣⲁⲙⲧ̄ etc.) without controlling parallel.

The reading specifies 'the living law of those who are good and those who are bitter'. Construction 'ⲡ + adj + ⲛⲟⲙⲟⲥ' takes ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ (5 chars, matching est_chars=5). Apposition with the preceding ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ on §642's first word makes this slightly redundant, hence not high.

ⲧⲁⲥ ⲅⲁⲣ {11} ⲁⲥϯ — between resumptive subject and verb of giving. Could be a relative converter, an emphatic copula, or a participial verb of sending; nothing in apparatus or parallel formula constrains the choice.

12 chars after 'she humbled the [archons / ⲛⲃⲉⲝⲉⲩⲉ]' before §645's 'and their cosmos'. Could be a coordinated noun phrase (e.g., 'and the powers') but the unfamiliar ⲛⲃⲉⲝⲉⲩⲉ already carries the weight; an honest non-restoration is preferable.
Editor's reading from line-end ⲧⲟⲩ + line-start ⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ is sound. 'Their substance and their cosmos' fits the Mother's humbling of the powers' essence and their world (the boundary-state).

'She poured upon {14} them' wants a possessed noun (heads, place, cosmos) of ~6 chars. The reading speaks of pouring 'in the boundary' but that comes after 'them there'. Multiple plausible fills, none uniquely constrained.
Single character before ⲛ̄ⲟⲁⲙ ('of/by might'); the only natural 1-char fill yielding 'ⲍⲛ̄ⲟⲁⲙ' = 'by might', exactly the formula of the fifth saying ('by might… the cosmos stands firm').

6-char slot between 'by might' and 'the cosmos stands firm'. The reading ascribes the cosmic standing-firm to the inmost Father's might. ⲙ̄ⲡⲓⲱⲧ fits length and sense, but other genitive nouns (ⲙ̄ⲡⲡⲛⲁ, ⲙ̄ⲡⲛⲁⲃ) would also fit.

9-char subject for 'all of them, they are one body, living'. The fifth saying gathers the four named realities (Father / Ambassador / Law / Mother). 'Their names then' (ⲛⲉⲩⲣⲉⲛ ⲇⲉ) ties §649's ⲙⲉⲗⲏⲩⲉ ('members') to the previously uttered five names. Fits length but not formulaically locked.

Preserved plural ending -ⲏⲩⲉ + 6 chars = ⲙⲉⲗⲏⲩⲉ exactly. Lexicon: ⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ = 'member / particular faculty in the spiritual organism'. The reading concludes precisely with 'discrete degrees [members] that exceed one another yet form one body' — the Grand-Man image.
